title: Model a step in its own interaction
statement: Model each step in the interaction learners will later use for it, because a step only narrated in the model leaves them performing a move they have never seen.
example: One design's model glowed 4 of 8 word tiles for the learner to tap and lock in, where the built model only narrated which words fit.
detail: A response to a review of a reading lesson found that its distinctive knowledge step was a tap-to-choose item in the independent task but only spoken narration in the model, so the child was modelled on prose and then asked to perform an interaction they had not seen (`grade3-reading/artifacts/Peter-Pan-L4-review-response-2026-08-25.pdf`, p.2). It called this the single change most likely to make the lesson feel like the skill it teaches, and committed to reusing the independent task's item in the model so that the model rehearses the move. The lesson's design had specified exactly that: its model has the learner tap each of 4 glowing words to lock it in (`grade3-reading/artifacts/pp1-v3-design.txt`, lines 157-159). A later gap register in the same course found two lessons handing the child a six-statement judging task cold, because the model's version of it had no engine primitive, and called the gap pedagogically real though mitigated (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/GAPS-2026-09-11.md`, lines 32-36).
against: Audits of later lessons in the same unit accepted narrated think-aloud models in place of the designs' interactive ones: "The doc's interactive-tap-to-find spec for the MM was already adapted to think_aloud convention arc-wide." (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/PEDAGOGY-L7-2026-09-05.md`, lines 25-26). The course standard lets the surface format change between stages while the operation stays the same: "Surface format may change only when the target operation remains demonstrably stable." (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, line 317). No learner outcome was measured either way.

evidence.quote: Our lesson has the KNOW bank in the child's independent task (p22, node step3, as an msq) but delivers it as spoken narration during the modelling. So the child is modelled on prose and then asked to perform an interaction they have not seen.
primitive already working at p22 step3, so the modelling rehearses the move the child must then make.
Correct / glowing set (4, auto-glow one by one; child taps each to lock it in): gloomy, miserable, unpleasant, strict.
Vocabulary chips (8, rendered as word tiles): gloomy · sunny · unpleasant · joyful · miserable · free · strict · exciting.
No engine primitive exists, so L6 and L7 hand the child the six-statement judging task cold.
but pedagogically real in the two lessons that carry the procedure.
